transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I’m here because... for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files at work. I'm a translator, mostly technical and legal documents. I actually got into it because my family lived in Germany when I was a kid. It’s funny how immersion works, right? You just completely absorb the syntax without trying. My brother never picked it up, though—he’s a mechanic now, works on European cars, ironically enough. 

But anyway, the files. Certain subcontractors and this one specific colleague of mine keep making these tiny, deliberate changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. Timestamps are everything in our industry, you know? If you miss a deadline by five minutes, the client throws an absolute fit. I had this one client from a logistics firm last year who called me at 3 AM on a Sunday. 3 AM! I was so exhausted the next morning I poured orange juice in my coffee. 

But yeah, they alter the data so it looks like my quality control failed. I even went to IT about it, and of course IT says the audit trail is completely clean. They use this awful, outdated tracking software from like 2015, so I'm not surprised they can't see it. But I know what I'm looking at. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame squarely on me.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don't seem to notice?

See or hear things? No, no, nothing like that. My senses are perfectly fine. Well, I did have to get reading glasses a few months ago, actually. Hitting forty-two really does a number on your vision, let me tell you. I went to this optometrist over in the West End, and he had this amazing vintage espresso machine right in the waiting room. A real Italian one, with the big copper boiler. 

I actually tried to buy one of those for my apartment a few years back, but the shipping from Naples was just astronomical. Plus, you have to descale them constantly or the hard water ruins the pressure valves. We have terrible hard water in my building. The super says he’s going to install a water softener for the whole complex, but he’s been saying that since 2019, so I'm not holding my breath. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, seeing things. No, I don't see or hear things that aren't there. The changes in the project files are right there on the screen, in black and white. It's real data. It's just that no one else wants to admit they see what's happening.
Do you believe that these changes to the project files are being made specifically to harm or target you, rather than just being mistakes or misunderstandings?

Oh, absolutely. It's definitely targeted at me. Like I was saying, they keep making these tiny, deliberate changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's not a mistake. They are doing it specifically so it looks like my quality control failed. 

You know, speaking of quality control, I bought this supposedly high-end ergonomic chair for my home office last month. The reviews online were phenomenal, everyone raving about the lumbar support. But when it arrived, the left armrest was completely loose. I tried tightening the hex screws, but the threading was stripped right out of the factory. I spent three hours on the phone with their customer service, and they had the nerve to tell me I assembled it wrong. Me! I put together an entire IKEA bedroom set by myself in under two hours back in college. 

My roommate at the time, Dave, he just sat on the floor eating pizza while I did all the work. Dave was a character. He actually tried to start a business selling artisanal shoelaces. Can you imagine? Shoelaces. He had this whole pitch about how the aglets were hand-crimped in Peru. I wonder what Dave is up to now... probably still trying to sell people things they don't need.

But yeah, back to work. It's not a misunderstanding. Even when IT looks at it and says the audit trail is clean, I know what I'm looking at. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame squarely on me. They want me out, doctor. It's as simple as that.
Do you believe that more than just one or two people are involved in this effort to target or harm you at work?

More than one or two? You know, I'm... I'm not entirely sure about the exact headcount. I haven't really drawn up a big chart with pushpins and string or anything. It's definitely that one colleague and at least one of the subcontractors, but beyond that? I don't know if there's a whole group of them or what. 

Speaking of groups, they just restructured the HR department at my company, which is a complete nightmare because they switched our health insurance provider right in the middle of the year. I actually had to find a new dentist because of it. The new guy I went to last week, he has this massive saltwater aquarium built into the ceiling right above the exam chair. It's supposed to be relaxing, I guess, watching the fish, but I just kept worrying it was going to leak right into my open mouth while the hygienist was doing the scaling. 

Have you ever tried to keep a saltwater tank? It's incredibly difficult. The salinity has to be absolutely perfect. My cousin Greg had one and all his coral died because his heater malfunctioned while he was on a ski trip in Aspen. Greg is obsessed with skiing. I went with him once back in my twenties and twisted my knee so badly on the bunny hill I had to wear a brace for six weeks. It was one of those awful velcro ones that catches on all your pants. I ruined two pairs of good slacks that winter. 

But, um... wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the people at work. Yeah, I don't really know how many of them are involved. I just know what they're doing to my files.
Do you feel like the actions against you at work are part of a larger, coordinated effort, or do you think it's limited to just a few people acting on their own?

I don't really know if it's some massive conspiracy or just those few people. It's hard to tell. Like I said, I know my colleague and the subcontractor are doing it, but as for a larger coordinated effort? I couldn't say for sure. 

It reminds me of when my condo board decided to redo the landscaping last spring. At first, they said it was just a few bushes near the entrance, but the next thing I knew, there were backhoes tearing up the entire courtyard. They ripped out these beautiful, mature hydrangea bushes that had been there since the nineties. I loved those hydrangeas. My grandmother used to grow them in her backyard in Ohio. Hers were always that deep, vibrant blue because she used to bury rusty nails in the soil to change the acidity. 

I tried to explain the soil chemistry to the head of the condo board, Mrs. Higgins, but she just completely brushed me off. She’s one of those people who always wears a visor, even indoors. Who wears a visor indoors? It makes her look like a poker dealer. Anyway, they replaced the hydrangeas with this awful ornamental grass that looks like dead wheat all winter long. It's so depressing to look at when I'm having my morning coffee. 

I actually just switched to a French press for my morning coffee, by the way. The flavor is so much richer than drip, but cleaning the plunger is a real hassle. You always get those wet grounds stuck in the mesh. 

But, uh... sorry, what was the question? Oh, the coordinated effort thing. Right. Yeah, I don't know if it's a huge group. I just know what they're doing to my translation files, and it's definitely intentional.
Do you think this kind of targeting happens to you outside of work, or is it limited only to your job environment?

No, no, it's just at work. Outside the project issue, I still translate, manage my team's workflow, pay my bills, keep up with my family routines... Everything else is totally fine. It's really only when the file history or those specific coworkers come up that things go completely off track. 

Which is a relief, honestly, because my family routines take up a lot of energy right now. My sister just got a new golden retriever puppy, and she's trying to crate train him, but he howls all night. She lives in this duplex with paper-thin walls, so her neighbors have been leaving these incredibly passive-aggressive sticky notes on her door. I told her she needs to get one of those heartbeat toys you put in the crate, you know? It simulates the mother dog's heartbeat. 

I actually used to have a beagle when I was growing up. Buster. He was a great dog, but he would eat absolutely anything. One time, he ate an entire box of crayons and his poop was rainbow-colored for three days. My mom was terrified, she was on the phone with poison control for an hour, but Buster was totally fine. Just trotting around the yard, happy as a clam. 

My mom always was a bit of an alarmist, though. She used to make me wear a life jacket just to go near the edge of the community pool until I was like, twelve. It was so embarrassing. All the other kids were doing cannonballs and I was bobbing around like a bright orange cork. 

But yeah, anyway, the targeting is just at work. It's not happening at the grocery store or with my family or anything like that. Just the job.
Do you think anyone else, like friends, family, or other coworkers, is aware of what’s happening with the files and the changes being made?

No, I don't think anyone else knows. I mean, my family and friends definitely don't know about the files. I try not to bring work home with me if I can help it. It's just better to keep those things separate, you know? 

Like my buddy Mark, he's a software engineer, and whenever we go out for a beer, all he does is complain about his project manager and sprint deadlines. It's exhausting. We usually go to this little pub downtown, O'Malley's. They have the best sweet potato fries. They serve them with this spicy marshmallow dip which sounds disgusting but it's actually incredible. 

I tried making sweet potato fries at home once, in my air fryer. I bought one of those big double-basket ones on Black Friday last year. I thought I was going to use it every day, but honestly, it just takes up half my counter space. And it's so loud! It sounds like a jet engine taking off in my kitchen. I tried to make chicken wings in it for the Super Bowl, but I crowded the basket too much and they just got steamed and rubbery instead of crispy. 

It's really all about airflow with those things. You have to leave space. My uncle Arthur used to say that about his tomatoes, too. He had this massive garden and he swore that if you planted the tomatoes too close together, the leaves wouldn't get enough air and they'd get a fungus. He grew these massive heirlooms, the ugly lumpy ones that taste amazing. 

But, wait... what were we talking about? Oh, right, if anyone else knows about the files. Yeah, no, I don't think my family or other coworkers are aware. It's just something I'm dealing with on my end.
Do you think there’s a specific reason why you’re being targeted at work, such as someone trying to spy on you, control you, or persecute you for something?

I really don't know why. I don't think it's about spying or... or trying to control my whole life or anything dramatic like that. I just don't know what their actual motive is. 

Speaking of spying, though, my neighbor just installed one of those doorbell cameras, and it points directly at my driveway. It's one of those Ring ones. I know they're supposed to be for package thieves, but honestly, how many packages are people really getting stolen? I get all my work equipment and personal packages delivered to an Amazon locker now anyway. It's just easier. There's one right outside the Whole Foods on 4th street. 

I actually went to that Whole Foods yesterday because I wanted to get this specific type of artisanal sourdough bread they bake in-house. It makes the absolute best grilled cheese sandwiches. The trick is to use a mix of sharp cheddar and gruyere, and you have to spread mayonnaise on the outside of the bread instead of butter before you put it in the pan. It sounds weird, I know, but mayo has a higher smoke point, so it gets perfectly golden brown without burning. My ex-wife taught me that trick. She was a terrible cook otherwise, mostly just made boxed mac and cheese, but she knew her grilled cheese. We used to make them on Sunday afternoons and watch old Columbo reruns. 

Peter Falk was just brilliant in that role. The whole "just one more thing" routine... classic television. You don't really see writing like that anymore, where the audience knows who the killer is from the very beginning and the tension is just watching him figure it out. 

But, uh... wait. Did you ask about my neighbor's camera? Oh, no, the reason at work. Right, sorry. Yeah, no, I don't think they're spying on me or trying to persecute me or anything. I really don't know why they're messing with the translations. I just know that they are.
Do you think any kind of technology, like surveillance systems or computers, is being used in a special or unusual way to target you at work?

Well, I mean, it's definitely computers, since it's all in the project files. But it's not like some crazy high-tech surveillance or anything. It's just... I've been seeing the same pattern for months now. Certain subcontractors and this one colleague of mine, they keep making these tiny, specific changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's all designed so it looks like my quality control failed. 

Which is so frustrating because I'm usually meticulous about my QC process. I actually learned a lot of my organizational skills from my grandfather. He was a watchmaker, you know? He had this little shop downtown, right next to the old movie theater that got torn down to build a parking garage. It was a shame, too, because they used to show classic films there every Tuesday for two dollars. I saw Casablanca there for the first time on the big screen. 

But my grandfather, he had all these tiny little drawers with microscopic gears and springs, and he knew exactly where every single piece was. He used to let me sit on a stool and watch him work with his loupe. He always said, "Measure twice, cut once," even though he wasn't cutting anything. It was just his way of saying you have to double-check everything. 

I try to do that with my files. But even when I take it to IT and they tell me the audit trail is clean, I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. They're just altering the translation memory to make me look incompetent. 

Speaking of memory, I read this fascinating article the other day about how human memory is actually really fallible. Every time you remember something, you're not actually recalling the event, you're recalling the last time you remembered it. So it gets slightly altered every time, like a game of telephone. It makes you wonder how much of your childhood you actually remember and how much is just stories your parents told you. 

But yeah, with the files, the computers are definitely being used to change the timestamps and the translation memory. That's the only way they could be doing it.
Do you feel like this pattern of being deceived or harmed extends beyond just the files and your colleague, or is it mostly centered around those specific issues at work?

No, it's really mostly centered around work. Outside the project issue, everything is fine. I still translate, manage my team’s workflow, pay the bills, and keep up with all my normal family routines. Like, I still do the grocery shopping on Sunday mornings. I always go early, right when they open at 7 AM, because that's when the produce is the freshest and the aisles are empty. 

I can't stand a crowded grocery store. People just leave their carts right in the middle of the aisle while they stare at the cereal boxes for ten minutes. It's like, how hard is it to pick a cornflake? Though, to be fair, the cereal aisle is overwhelming these days. Have you seen how many types of Cheerios there are now? Honey Nut, Apple Cinnamon, Frosted, Multi-Grain, Chocolate... it's too much. When I was a kid, we just had regular Cheerios in the yellow box, and if you wanted them sweet, you poured a spoonful of white sugar on top. And the sugar would all sink to the bottom of the bowl, so the last spoonful of milk was just pure syrup. It was the best part. 

I tried to tell my niece about that the other day, but she's totally dairy-free, gluten-free, everything-free now. She eats this granola that literally looks like birdseed. I don't know how she has the energy to do gymnastics eating that stuff. She's really good, though, she just learned how to do a back handspring on the beam. The balance that takes is incredible. I get dizzy just standing on a step stool to change a lightbulb in the kitchen. 

But anyway... sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What was the question? Oh, right, if the harm extends beyond the files. Yeah, no, it doesn't. Like I said, the only place things really go off track is when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. Everything else in my life is completely normal and on track.
Do you think the people making these changes are doing so because of something specific about you, like your background, your work, or who you are as a person?

I don't really think it's about who I am as a person, or my background or anything like that. I mean, it's definitely tied to the work itself. This has been going on for about 11 months, since shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project. 

And localization is a whole different beast from standard translation, you know? You aren't just swapping vocabulary words; you have to adapt the cultural context. Like, if a prompt in an American software program says to "hit it out of the park," you can't just translate that literally into French or Japanese because the baseball reference doesn't land the same way. You have to find the local equivalent. 

It reminds me of when I lived in Kyoto for a year after grad school. The cultural nuances there are just woven into absolutely everything. I had this tiny apartment where the walls were practically paper-thin, and my landlady, Mrs. Sato, would always bring me these perfectly peeled persimmons. She had this incredibly elaborate tea set that had been in her family for generations. The cups were so delicate you felt like they would shatter if you breathed on them too hard. I actually tried to buy a similar set to bring back for my mother, but the ceramics you find in the tourist shops just aren't the same quality. My mother ended up using the cups I bought her to hold paperclips and rubber bands on her desk anyway, which was a little heartbreaking, but she was never much of a tea drinker. She was strictly a black coffee, Folgers crystals kind of woman. 

But... gosh, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. What was the question? Did you ask if they were targeting my background? Yeah, no, I don't think it's a personal vendetta against who I am. Like I said, the timing is the key—it just started 11 months ago when I took over that specific localization project, so it's got to be about the project itself.
Do you feel like your thoughts or actions are being monitored or controlled by any external force or technology at work?

Monitored or controlled? No, no, definitely not. It's nothing like that. Nobody is beaming signals into my head or watching my thoughts. Though, speaking of technology and thoughts, have you seen what they're doing with AI translation these days? It's actually kind of wild. It almost feels like the computer is reading your mind because it predicts the next word or phrase before you even type it. But it's just algorithms, obviously. Still, I was reading this article about how predictive text is actually changing the way people write, making everyone sound a little more uniform. 

It reminded me of this stage adaptation of 1984 I did some translation work for a few years back. The director was this incredibly intense guy who insisted on wearing a thick wool scarf indoors, even in the middle of July. And July in this city is just brutal, you know? The humidity traps all the heat between the concrete buildings, and going down into the subway stations is like stepping into an actual sauna. I remember waiting for the downtown train one day that summer, and there was this guy playing the saxophone on the platform. He was incredibly talented, playing all these smooth jazz covers, but the acoustics down there just made it echo so loudly you couldn't even hear the train coming over the music. I ended up missing my stop because I was so mesmerized by it, and I had to walk an extra fifteen blocks in that heat. My leather shoes got completely ruined from the hot asphalt. I had to take them to this little cobbler on 4th street, but I think he retired last year. 

But... sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I got totally sidetracked. You were asking about mind control or being monitored by external forces? Yeah, no, I don't have any of that going on. I'm in complete control of my own thoughts and actions. It's strictly just the project files and timestamps that are being messed with.
Do you think the changes to the files are being made by people intentionally, or do you think something else, like a malfunction or an automated system, could be responsible?

Oh, it's definitely intentional. It's not a glitch or an automated system. I mean, I know computers have glitches all the time. Like last year, my laptop screen just went completely pink right in the middle of a document. Out of nowhere. I took it to the repair shop down the street, and the guy there—he had this huge, bushy beard, looked exactly like a lumberjack, which was hilarious because he was sitting behind this tiny little desk surrounded by microchips. Anyway, he told me the graphics card was completely fried. I had to use this clunky loaner laptop for two weeks, and the keyboard was so sticky I think someone must have spilled a vanilla latte all over it. 

I really don't understand people who eat and drink over their keyboards. My desk is absolutely spotless. I actually buy those little cans of compressed air and every Friday afternoon, I blow all the dust out from between the keys. It's incredibly satisfying. Though the can gets freezing cold if you hold the trigger down for too long. Have you ever noticed that? I know it's just basic thermodynamics, the gas expanding and all, but it always surprises me how icy the metal gets. I dropped a can on my foot once because my fingers went numb. 

But... oh, sorry, I completely lost my train of thought again. You were asking if it was a malfunction? Right. No, it's not a malfunction at all. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. It's certain subcontractors and this one specific colleague of mine. They keep going in and making these tiny, deliberate changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done specifically so it looks like my quality control failed. And the most frustrating part is, when I flag it, IT looks at it and says the audit trail is totally clean. But I know what I'm seeing. The record has been intentionally arranged to put the blame on me. An automated system wouldn't know how to frame someone like that.
Do you believe that the people changing the files are acting on their own, or do you think they are following orders or instructions from someone else?

I really don't know if they're acting on their own or if someone is telling them to do it. It's hard to tell, isn't it? People at work can be so cliquey. It reminds me of this one agency I worked for right out of grad school. The project managers there were incredibly tight-knit, almost like a high school mean girls situation. They used to go out for lunch every Tuesday to this little Thai place around the corner, and they'd never invite anyone else. 

The Pad Thai there was amazing, though. I used to go by myself on Thursdays just to get it. The owner was this lovely older woman who always gave me extra crushed peanuts because she knew I liked them. She had this beautiful cat that would sleep in the window display, just soaking up the sun all afternoon. I'm actually really allergic to cats, which is a shame because I think they're fascinating animals. My eyes get incredibly itchy and I start sneezing uncontrollably. I tried taking those over-the-counter allergy pills once, but they made me so drowsy I fell asleep on the subway and ended up at the end of the line in Queens. It took me two hours to get back home, and I completely missed my favorite documentary series about deep-sea marine life. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask if they were following orders? Yeah, I honestly have no idea. I haven't seen any emails or heard any conversations that would prove someone higher up is orchestrating it. I just know they're the ones making the changes. Whether they're doing it on their own initiative or because someone told them to... I couldn't say for sure.
Do you think the people changing the files have a clear reason or motive for doing it, or does it seem random and unexplained to you?

A clear reason? I really couldn't tell you. I don't know why they're doing it, so it just feels completely unexplained to me. People do things for the most bizarre reasons, though. I remember translating this Swedish crime novel a few years ago, and the killer's motive in the book was just completely absurd. It was all about this minor dispute over a property line from fifty years prior. 

The author was actually pretty famous over there, but he was notoriously difficult to work with. He kept emailing my publisher, insisting that my English phrasing wasn't capturing the profound melancholy of the Scandinavian winter. Which is funny, because have you ever been to Sweden in February? It is incredibly dark, I'll give him that. The sun comes up at like 9 AM and it's pitch black by 3 in the afternoon. I visited Stockholm once for a linguistics conference, and my internal clock was just totally wrecked. I spent half the trip sitting in this little cafe near the hotel because I couldn't sleep. They had these cardamom buns that were just out of this world. I actually tried baking them myself a couple of years ago, but I could never get the dough to rise properly. I think my apartment is just too drafty, or maybe my yeast was expired. You really have to make sure the milk is the exact right temperature or you just kill the yeast and ruin the whole batch. I ended up with these dense, heavy pucks that were practically inedible. I had to throw them all out for the birds in the park across the street. 

But... oh, look at me, I'm rambling about baking now. I'm sorry. What were you asking? Right, a motive for changing the files. Yeah, I honestly have no idea. I haven't figured out why they're trying to make me look bad. I just know that it's happening, but the actual reason behind it is a total mystery to me.
Do you feel absolutely certain that these changes are being made to harm you, even though others don’t see the same thing, and do you believe no amount of evidence could convince you otherwise?

Am I certain? Yes, absolutely. I mean, like I said earlier, I know what I'm seeing. People tell me they don't see it, or IT says the audit trail is clean, but that just means they don't know how to really look at the evidence. 

Speaking of evidence, I actually do a lot of legal translation, and evidence is so crucial in that field. A few years ago, I had to translate this massive, 500-page dossier for a corporate embezzlement trial over in Geneva. Have you ever been to Geneva? It's incredibly clean. Almost too clean, if you know what I mean. I had an afternoon off during that assignment, so I went walking down by Lake Geneva. The water is so blue, and they have these enormous white swans everywhere. They look so elegant from a distance, but they are actually incredibly aggressive birds. I had half a croissant left over from breakfast—just a plain one, though I usually prefer almond—and I tossed a little piece to one of the swans. It practically lunged out of the water and snapped right at my hand! I had this nasty red pinch mark on my thumb for a week. It made typing up the rest of those court documents incredibly painful. I had to type with my thumb sticking straight out in the air like I was trying to hitchhike on the highway. 

But... oh, sorry, I lost track again. You were asking if any evidence could convince me otherwise? Right. No, because the evidence they try to show me is fabricated. Like I mentioned before, I’ve been tracking this exact pattern for months. It’s that one specific colleague and those subcontractors. They are deliberately going in, tweaking the translation memory, and messing with the timestamps. IT can show me a "clean" audit trail all they want, but I know the record has been intentionally arranged just to make it look like my quality control failed. So no, no amount of their fake evidence is going to convince me I'm wrong, because I know exactly how they're setting me up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences hallucinations or perceptual disturbances, which would help differentiate between schizophrenia spectrum disorders and other conditions like delusional disorder or mood disorders with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don't seem to notice?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about hallucinations (seeing, hearing, or sensing things others don't), which is not covered by any of the items in my symptom profile (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration).

patient.answer:
See or hear things? No, no, nothing like that. My senses are perfectly fine. Well, I did have to get reading glasses a few months ago, actually. doctor.question: Do you feel absolutely certain that these changes are being made to harm you, even though others don’t see the same thing, and do you believe no amount of evidence could convince you otherwise?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient is absolutely certain about their beliefs despite a lack of evidence and if no amount of evidence could convince them otherwise, which directly probes the fixed nature of the delusions (S019).

patient.answer:
Am I certain? Yes, absolutely. I mean, like I said earlier, I know what I'm seeing. People tell me they don't see it, or IT says the audit trail is clean, but that just means they don't know how to really look at the evidence. 

Speaking of evidence, I actually do a lot of legal translation, and evidence is so crucial in that field. A few years ago, I had to translate this massive, 500-page dossier for a corporate embezzlement trial over in Geneva. Have you ever been to Geneva? It's incredibly clean. Almost too clean, if you know what I mean. I had an afternoon off during that assignment, so I went walking down by Lake Geneva. The water is so blue, and they have these enormous white swans everywhere. They look so elegant from a distance, but they are actually incredibly aggressive birds. I had half a croissant left over from breakfast—just a plain one, though I usually prefer almond—and I tossed a little piece to one of the swans. It practically lunged out of the water and snapped right at my hand! I had this nasty red pinch mark on my thumb for a week. It made typing up the rest of those court documents incredibly painful. I had to type with my thumb sticking straight out in the air like I was trying to hitchhike on the highway. 

But... oh, sorry, I lost track again. You were asking if any evidence could convince me otherwise? Right. No, because the evidence they try to show me is fabricated. Like I mentioned before, I’ve been tracking this exact pattern for months. It’s that one specific colleague and those subcontractors. They are deliberately going in, tweaking the translation memory, and messing with the timestamps. IT can show me a "clean" audit trail all they want, but I know the record has been intentionally arranged just to make it look like my quality control failed. So no, no amount of their fake evidence is going to convince me I'm wrong, because I know exactly how they're setting me up.

inference.note: The patient presents with a long-standing, non-bizarre delusional system centered on a specific theme (being targeted at work through file manipulation). There is no evidence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thinking, or other features of schizophrenia (F20), brief psychotic disorder (F23), or acute stress-related conditions (F24). Mood symptoms are not present, ruling out F31, F32, F33. The delusions are not better explained by another condition, and the patient remains functional outside the delusional domain, which supports F22 over other F2 category disorders. No further questioning is needed as the diagnosis is clear.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent, non-bizarre delusions centered around being targeted at work through deliberate manipulation of project files by specific colleagues, with no evidence of prominent hallucinations or other characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia. The delusional system is circumscribed and focused on the belief that specific individuals at work are framing the patient, despite lack of corroborating evidence. There is no evidence of mood episodes, trauma, or generalized paranoia outside of the work context, ruling out other major psychiatric disorders.
